subject.title: fix(agents): prevent recursive task execution during model fallback

question: Should a fallback model handling a completion announcement lose all work-spawning capability until a new user turn, or must it retain `sessions_spawn` for legitimate remaining steps unrelated to the announced result?
rationale: The current invariant forbids replaying completed work, but the patch implements a broader capability removal that changes existing fallback behavior; source inspection cannot determine whether that compatibility loss is intended product policy.

options.title: Narrow the guard
options.body: Preserve legitimate original-task follow-up spawns while mechanically rejecting re-execution or re-delegation of the announced completed work, with positive and negative regression coverage.

options.title: Adopt read-only completion turns
options.body: Keep the blanket spawn prohibition, but explicitly approve the compatibility change and align announcement wording, docs, errors, and tests with that read-only policy.

options.title: Land prompt mitigation only
options.body: Remove the mechanical tool ban from this PR and track a generalized delegation-policy design on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Narrow the guard
recommendation.body: Preserve legitimate original-task follow-up spawns while mechanically rejecting re-execution or re-delegation of the announced completed work, with positive and negative regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc authored the cross-harness review that established the invariant and is the clearest available owner for deciding its compatibility boundary.
